rows.stem: For an event E, \(P(E) + P(\overline{E}) = x\), then the value of \(x^2 - 3\) is :
rows.solution:
An event and its complement together cover every outcome, so \(P(E) + P(\overline{E}) = 1\) and \(x = 1\).

\(x^2 - 3 = 1 - 3 = -2\), which is option (A) \(-2\).

rows.stem: The first term of an AP is \(p\) and the common difference is \(q\), then its 10th term is :
rows.solution:
The nth term of an AP is \(a_n = a + (n - 1)d\). With \(a = p\) and \(d = q\):

\(a_{10} = p + 9q\), which is option (C) \(p + 9q\).

rows.stem:
Shown below are three triangles. The measures of two adjacent sides and included angle are given for each triangle :

Which of these triangles are similar ?

options.label: D
options.text: \(\Delta RPQ\), \(\Delta XZY\) and \(\Delta MNL\) are similar to one another

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - three triangles drawn side by side: PQR with PR = 6 cm, PQ = 4 cm and angle P = 60 degrees; XYZ with ZX = 9 cm, ZY = 6 cm and angle Z = 60 degrees; LMN with NL = 3 cm, NM = 4 cm and angle N = 60 degrees. Every side and angle is given only on the drawing. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
Compare the two sides that include the \(60^\circ\) angle in each triangle.

In triangle RPQ the sides at P are \(PR = 6\) cm and \(PQ = 4\) cm; in triangle XZY the sides at Z are \(ZX = 9\) cm and \(ZY = 6\) cm.

\(\dfrac{PR}{ZX} = \dfrac{6}{9} = \dfrac{2}{3}\) and \(\dfrac{PQ}{ZY} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), and \(\angle P = \angle Z = 60^\circ\). So by the SAS similarity criterion \(\Delta RPQ \sim \Delta XZY\).

In triangle MNL the sides at N are 3 cm and 4 cm. Their ratio \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) (or \(\dfrac{4}{3}\)) does not match \(\dfrac{6}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}\), so triangle MNL is not similar to the other two.

This is option (A) \(\Delta RPQ\) and \(\Delta XZY\).

rows.stem: If \(\cos y = 0\), then what is the value of \(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos\dfrac{y}{2}\) ?
rows.solution:
\(\cos y = 0\) gives \(y = 90^\circ\), so \(\dfrac{y}{2} = 45^\circ\) and \(\cos 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

\(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos\dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, a circle with centre O is inscribed inside \(\Delta LMN\). A and B are the points of tangency. Find \(\angle ANB\).
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - triangle LMN with its incircle (centre O) touching LN at A and MN at B; the radii OA and OB are drawn and the reflex angle AOB is marked 240 degrees. That 240 degree value appears only on the drawing. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
The reflex angle AOB is \(240^\circ\), so \(\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 240^\circ = 120^\circ\).

The radii OA and OB are perpendicular to the tangents NL and NM at the points of contact, so \(\angle OAN = \angle OBN = 90^\circ\).

The angles of the quadrilateral OANB add up to \(360^\circ\):

\(\angle ANB = 360^\circ - (90^\circ + 90^\circ + 120^\circ) = 60^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial \(x^2 + 7x + 10\), and verify the relationship between the zeroes and its coefficients.
rows.solution:
\(x^2 + 7x + 10 = x^2 + 2x + 5x + 10 = (x + 2)(x + 5)\), so the zeroes are \(-2\) and \(-5\).

Here \(a = 1\), \(b = 7\), \(c = 10\).

Sum of the zeroes \(= -2 + (-5) = -7 = \dfrac{-7}{1} = -\dfrac{b}{a}\), that is \(-\dfrac{\text{coefficient of } x}{\text{coefficient of } x^2}\).

Product of the zeroes \(= (-2) \times (-5) = 10 = \dfrac{10}{1} = \dfrac{c}{a}\), that is \(\dfrac{\text{constant term}}{\text{coefficient of } x^2}\).

So the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients is verified.

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: Parthi and Alisha found a treasure that is exactly on the straight line joining their locations. Parthi’s location is at point \((-6, -5)\) and Alisha’s location is at point \((10, 11)\). The distance from the treasure to Parthi’s location is three times that of the distance to Alisha’s location. Find the coordinates of the location of the treasure.
rows.solution:
Let Parthi be at \(P(-6, -5)\), Alisha at \((10, 11)\) and the treasure at \(T(x, y)\) on the line between them.

The distance from T to Parthi is three times the distance from T to Alisha, so T divides the segment from Parthi to Alisha in the ratio \(3 : 1\).

By the section formula:

\(x = \dfrac{3 \times 10 + 1 \times (-6)}{3 + 1} = \dfrac{24}{4} = 6\), and \(y = \dfrac{3 \times 11 + 1 \times (-5)}{3 + 1} = \dfrac{28}{4} = 7\).

The treasure is at \((6, 7)\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem: Two sections, A and B, of class X contributed a total of ₹ 1500 for the Uttarakhand flood victims. The contribution from X-A was ₹ 100 less than that of X-B. Graphically, find the amounts contributed by both sections.
rows.solution:
Let the contributions of X-A and X-B be ₹ \(x\) and ₹ \(y\).

Together they gave ₹ 1500: \(x + y = 1500\) ... (i)

X-A gave ₹ 100 less than X-B: \(x = y - 100\), that is \(y - x = 100\) ... (ii)

Points on \(x + y = 1500\), that is \(y = 1500 - x\):

| \(x\) | 0 | 500 | 1000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 1500 | 1000 | 500 |

Points on \(y - x = 100\), that is \(y = x + 100\):

| \(x\) | 0 | 500 | 1000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 100 | 600 | 1100 |

Plot these points on the same axes (a scale such as 1 unit for ₹ 100 works) and draw the two lines. They intersect at the point \((700, 800)\).

(Check: \(700 + 800 = 1500\) and \(800 - 700 = 100\).)

So section X-A contributed ₹ 700 and section X-B contributed ₹ 800.
